newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Perry, in letter, reassures Balts on NATO.
newsitem.headline: Perry, in letter, reassures Balts on NATO.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry, who dismayed the three Baltic states by saying they were not yet ready for NATO, has reassured them in a letter that they are "fully eligible" for membership of the alliance.
The Lithuanian Defence Ministry confirmed the existence of the letter, which was reported by Lithuanian daily Lietuvos rytas. A copy was made available to Reuters.

Perry, speaking last month at a defence ministers meeting in Norway, said Lithuania and Baltic neighbours Latvia and Estonia were not yet ready for NATO as they did not have the capability to come to the defence of other NATO members.

It was the first open admission by a U.S. policy maker that the Balts were unlikely to be included in an early expansion of the alliance to take in former Communist-bloc countries although NATO diplomats had said it quietly for some time.
The Balts, independent from the former Soviet Union since 1991, are anxious for strong security guarantees to make sure they never again come under the domination of Russia.

"I underscore that I said, and I believe, that the Balts are fully eligible for NATO membership and that I look forward to the day when each country is a member," Perry said in the letter, which was dated October 3.
In the letter, Perry said "some press reports and diplomatic chatter" had put an incorrect intepretation on his words.
He said the media focussed on the negative aspect of his comments on the Balts' preparedness for the alliance, which he said were made in a "spirit of realism and practicality".
He said that although the Balts were not ready at the moment, the U.S. would work with them to get their defence capability up to alliance standards.
"The U.S. has led in supporting the independence and security of the Baltic countries. The DoD (U.S. Department of Defence) and I share fully in that commitment," the letter said.
"I look forward to continuing work with you and the other Baltic ministers to help prepare your nations and defence establishments to assume the responsibilities of NATO membership," Perry added.
